newsitem.title: USA: Bangor Hydro does not declare qlty div.
newsitem.headline: Bangor Hydro does not declare qlty div.

text.p: Bangor Hydro-Electric Co said Wednesday its board of directors did not declare a quarterly dividend on its common stock because of financial difficulties.
The company said the board decided to suspend the payout, which had been $0.18 a share quarterly, due to difficulties at the Maine Yankee nuclear generating plant.
"Maine Yankee has experienced a series of problems and is presently off-line until at least mid-summer," it said, explaining how it was buying replacement power at market prices.

Other reasons included the lack of adequate earnings, the need to conserve cash, and the need to manage the potential for being unable to comply with covenants in loan agreements with its lenders, it said.
The company, which reduced the quarterly dividend to $0.18 a share from $0.33 in the second quarter of 1995, also said it was seeking permission to raise its rates.
It owns seven percent of Maine Yankee, which provides almost a quarter of its power supply requirement.
Bangor Hydro did declare quarterly dividends on its 8.76 percent, seven percent, 4.25 percent and four percent preferred stocks.
